title: Wildclaw: Colossus Hunt
observed_goal: At the menu frame, the goal is presented as “Track it. Climb it. Bring it down.” along with selecting a quarry/target to begin the hunt; execution of the hunt, climbing, or bringing it down was not observed in the frames.
observed_controls: In the page/menu text: WASD for movement, Mouse for looking, Shift for Sprint / Brace, Space for Dodge roll, LMB for Slash combo, RMB (hold) for Charged slash, E for Grapple / Ride, C for Lock-on camera, R for Drink potion, F for Gather / Resupply, and Esc for Pause.
These are interface commands/text; none was confirmed with an observable result during active gameplay execution.

Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, and holding ArrowRight + Space for 900 milliseconds were attempted in the input capture, but game-like acceptance of these inputs was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
observed_core_loop: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; the current frames remain in a loading state, while the fallback frames show the target-selection menu rather than a hunt, engagement, climb, attack, and outcome loop.
progress_feedback: The screenshot shows loading percentages of 12%, 26%, and 32%, and the page text records 9%, 26%, and 32% respectively; the percentage change may simply reflect the passage of time/loading and does not establish game progress or input acceptance. In the menu, the target status is “Not yet hunted.”
decisions_risk_reward: The page menu shows three quarries with different threat levels and the status “Not yet hunted,” so target selection is likely a decision involving different threat levels; actual risk/reward and the consequences of selection were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive during game execution.
rewards: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no reward, score, rank, loot, or hunt outcome is visible in the frames.
penalties_failure: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no failure, damage, death, cost, or direct penalty is visible in the frames.
outcomes_replay: not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no win, loss, hunt ending, return to the menu, or repeating loop was recorded.
onboarding: The loading page shows one tip about dodge timing and one tip about holding heavy attack. The fallback menu displays a control list and an explanation that the mouse is captured after Begin Hunt; interactive instruction or confirmation that the controls were understood was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
visual_audio_accessibility: The screenshots show a legible menu interface with a 3D environmental background and a large creature, target-selection cards, a Begin Hunt button, and a controls panel. Audio was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; accessibility status, subtitles, contrast settings, or remapping were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive in this evidence.
technical_clues: The metadata records one page at 200 and three canvases sized 1280×800; this is only a technical clue about page structure, not proof of complete game execution.

Resource totals include 5 scripts, 47 images, 40 fetches, and one xhr; script_count_scanned equals 0 and engine_markers and tuning_constant_candidates are empty, so no conclusion is drawn about the engine or game logic.

A console warning concerning software WebGL fallback, several 403/400 errors, and a remote config error were recorded; their effect on the game was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.

Changes in the loading frames and the creature’s movement/state change in two fallback frames show only an image change or passage of time; according to the metadata, visual change alone does not prove that input was understood or accepted.
transferable_principles: Present the objective and selection status briefly and visibly before interaction begins.
Show the controls and expected feedback explicitly and unambiguously at the same point where the user is ready to start.
Keep threat-level decisions separate from actual outcomes, and make the consequences of selection understandable through direct feedback.
For a claim of interactive success, do not rely on a temporal or visual change; a repeatable loop and outcome are required.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, every score/rank should reflect skill and performance only, not a purchase or wallet, and not a paid advantage.
If the target/threat idea is used, turn it into a legible, skill-based decision and do not create an economic advantage or purchasable asset.

The control scheme should remain without free brake, horizontal direction change, or a branching path requiring new controls; each of these is only a hypothesis requiring separate testing, not a conclusion from this game.
From this evidence, only onboarding clarity and separation of selection status from actual execution can be transferred; the hunt loop or its controls cannot be transferred as confirmed facts.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce or propose this game’s names, characters, creatures, art, environment, level, text, audio, brand, or assets.
Do not report the official card’s claim about tracking, climbing, grappling, and striking vital points as observed execution.
Do not use a change in the loading percentage or a difference between two frames to prove input acceptance, the existence of a loop, or an outcome.
Do not treat the absence of an element in the opening frame as evidence that it is absent from the entire game.

evidence.claim: The load, after_start, and after_key_burst frames show a loading page with the game title, a tip, and a loading percentage; no active gameplay is visible in them.
The recorded page text during the loading stages includes a tip about Flow Evade and charging heavy attack/True Slash.
The after_combined_input frame shows the quarry-selection menu, three “Not yet hunted” statuses, Begin Hunt, Field Guide, Settings, Enemy Library, and the controls panel.
The late frame shows the same selection menu and controls panel; the creature’s changed position in the background, without a loop or outcome, does not prove input execution.
The page says that Begin Hunt captures the mouse for camera control and Esc releases it, and provides the WASD/Mouse/Shift/Space/LMB/RMB/E/C/R/F/Esc control list.
The official game card claims tracking giant creatures, dodging attacks, grappling aboard, and striking vital points; this claim was not playtested through game execution in the frames.
The metadata records 403/400 errors, a remote config error, a software WebGL fallback warning, three canvases, and no engine markers; the gameplay effect of these clues is unclear.

limitations: The capture record is partial. The current stages show only loading; after_combined_input and late are from fallback-1, and the metadata says screenshots for those stages timed out. Execution of the hunt, camera control, attack, grapple, dodge, damage, reward, failure, win/loss, and replay was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. A change between two frames alone does not establish input acceptance, and the absence of an element in the opening frame does not establish its absence from the entire game.
